name: – Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the Union, of the Protocol on the implementation of the Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the European Union and the Government of the Cook Islands (2025-2032)
part_text:
The European Parliament approves a new seven-year fishing deal between the European Union and the Cook Islands, a small Pacific island country. It lets four EU tuna boats fish there for 40 days a year. In return, the EU pays 460,000 euros a year: 165,000 for fishing access and 295,000 to support the islands' own sustainable fishing policy. The deal also aims to strengthen scientific cooperation and the EU's partnerships in the region.

- Four EU tuna boats get 40 fishing days a year in Cook Islands waters.
- The Cook Islands receive 460,000 euros a year, mostly for their fishing policy.
- The deal applies provisionally since December 2025; Parliament's approval lets it enter into force.
